0

Summary

The Federal Reserve Board (Board) provides students opportunities for career success. The Board’s Internship program is designed to provide valuable work experience for undergraduate and graduate students considering careers including, but not limited to, economics, finance and accounting, information systems, and data analysis. The Board believes that by combining academic endeavors with project-related work experience, qualified and capable college students can gain the practical knowledge need in a competitive global job market. Internships are paid positions with salaries commensurate with credit hours; internships may be in-person, remote or hybrid, depending on the needs of the team. Employment in the Board’s internship program is granted to U.S. citizens. Applicants must be currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree program at an accredited university and returning to continue studies after the internship. Interns receive a syllabus or research project plan outlining their projects and goals for the internship. Interns are assigned a supervisor or mentor to guide them through their internship, and regular check-in meetings with their manager to manage performance expectations and assist with learning goals. Interns have access to a wide range of training programs and events for professional development purposes.

About the Division and Section/Team:  

The Administration (ADM) section within the Division of Research & Statistics (R&S) provides strategic guidance and operational support across the division in areas of human resources, training and development, budget, compensation, recruitment, and outreach. 

 

About the Role:  

ADM is seeking an undergraduate intern (rising senior) interested in a well-rounded, hands-on internship experience across multiple HR functions. The intern will work on key initiatives including onboarding, training, outreach, recruiting, data analysis, and operations (budget, procurement, office space management, etc.).  

This internship is designed to be both educational and practical, preparing the intern for post-graduation roles in the private or public sector. 

 

Examples of summer projects include:  

  • Event Execution: Coordinate intern summer events, support division orientation, and help facilitate professional development sessions 
  • Data Analysis: Conduct process evaluations and develop recommendations for improvements 
  • Operations: Support budget tracking, procurement workflows, recruiting coordination, and office space management 
  • Content Creation: Develop presentations, recruiting materials, and leadership-ready deliverables 

 

Requirements/Background: 

  • Rising senior currently enrolled in an undergraduate degree program in Organizational Development, Human Resources, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, Business Management, Accounting/Finance, Information Systems, Instructional Design, or a related field 
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills 
  • Project management, organization, and time management skills 
  • Ability to learn quickly with attention to detail, proactive mindset, and adaptability 
  • Must be able to work full-time for 10-12 weeks in Washington, D.C. 

 

Preferred: 

  • Prior internship or work experience 
  • Leadership and/or event planning experience 
  • Data analytics/visualization skills 
  • Cross-functional collaboration experience 
  • Experience presenting to large audiences 
  • Familiarity with survey tools (Qualtrics, Forms) 

 

Required Documents for Application:  

  • Resume 
  • Undergraduate Unofficial Transcripts 

 

Location: This position requires an onsite presence at our offices in Washington, D.C.  

 

Note: U.S. Citizenship is required. Applicants must be current students, graduating from their program August 2027 or later. Proof of enrollment will be required.  

Keywords: leadership, human resources, management, event planning  


Learn more about our internship program: https://www.federalreserve.gov/careers-internships.htm
